title: Rollback Simulation Layer and Fallback Topology Validator for Deployments
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We rely on canary rollouts, A/B tests and shadow traffic for safe model deployments, but we lack a deterministic preflight that simulates realistic failure modes (region outage, capacity tier exhaustion, model variant mismatch) and validates the routing+fallback topology that will be used in production. This causes surprises during rollouts and manual interventions to trigger rollbacks or reconfigure routing policies.

Goal: Build a Rollback Simulation Layer (RSL) and a Fallback Topology Validator (FTV) that: 1) Simulates outages and capacity/tier degradations against a proposed deployment topology (canary weights, shadow routes, region priorities, tier preferences); 2) Runs compatibility and semantic checks between model variants used in primary and fallback paths; 3) Produces a deterministic pass/fail preflight report and suggested auto-rollback triggers that can be applied in Console/CI before or during rollout.

Why this ticket: This is an infrastructure + tooling investment to reduce human toil and decrease MTTR during problematic rollouts. It ties into the rollout service, routing policy compiler, and the Console UI preflight flow.

Scope (MVP):
- A simulation harness that can run three failure scenarios: regional outage, dedicated-capacity-tier-saturation, and KV-cache-compatibility-failure.
- Validator rules that check for: model IO/schema compatibility, KV cache key name collisions across variants, quantization profile compatibility (fallback-able?), and latency headroom under synthetic load.
- A pass/fail preflight report plus structured suggestions (e.g., "increase fallback replica count", "pin quantization to int8-compatible variant", "add region-level fallback to eu-west") that are human-readable.
- Integration hooks to: rollout-controller (to gate executes), Console (preflight button with report), and CI (a new job that can be added to model deployment pipelines).

Out of scope: automated rollout changes (we will surface suggestions; auto-mutating topology will be a follow-up once safeties are proven).
acceptance_criteria: Preflight run can be executed from Console and returns within 180s for a standard canary topology
Simulation harness can reproduce at least three failure scenarios deterministically
FTV flags mismatches for model IO shape, missing tokenizer metadata, and incompatible quant profiles
Report contains clear remediation suggestions and references relevant PRs/configs
Integration tests in CI that run the RSL against a mocked rollout-controller and pass in 90% of baseline cases
comments: 2026-01-19 - Priya Shah: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/RSL+-+Design (see Design v1). Agreed MVP scenarios and ownership (Serving: Eric, Routing: Mei, Console: Jonah).

2026-01-25 - Eric Nguyen: Spike complete. Implemented a minimal simulator that can flip 'region-up' flags and replay recorded traffic patterns. POC repository: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rsl/tree/spike. Observed that some model variants rely on legacy tokenizer keys which break shadowing; added initial compatibility checks.

2026-01-29 - Mei Chen: Router policy compiler needs a small API change to export 'fallback topology' as structured JSON. Filed ENG-47298 to track the compiler change and ensure CI artifacts include topology snapshots.

2026-02-02 - Design review (Jonah Kim): UX for preflight report needs to highlight 'safety score' and recommended next steps; design spec link: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/rsl-preflight-v1.pdf. Jonah approved MVP layout with minor copy edits.

2026-02-06 - Eric Nguyen: First integration test wired into CircleCI: runs RSL against a stubbed rollout-controller and asserts report contains remediation suggestions. Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1124 (awaiting codeowners approval).

2026-02-10 - Priya Shah: Product acceptance: running a sample canary (chat-llama-v2 -> chat-llama-v2-int8 fallback) shows FTV flagging quantization mismatch and recommended 'pin int8-fallback and increase fallback replicas to 2'. Planning rollout to internal infra next week.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full-fidelity traffic replay is expensive (needs historical KV/cache); MVP uses sampled synthetic traffic + recorded traces. We prioritized deterministic failure injection over full traffic fidelity to keep CI cost reasonable. Future: add probabilistic stochastic replay for edge-case latency regressions.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Spike: simulator + simple compatibility checks (completed)
Phase 2 - Validator and report generation, Console preflight UI hook (in progress)
Phase 3 - CI integration and internal dogfood, run against 10 recent rollouts
Phase 4 - Evaluate automation for partial auto-rollback (follow-up ticket)
